hot.title: Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: The authors introduce targeted guidance for multi-turn software-engineering reinforcement learning, placing textual feedback before a failing turn and distilling the same model’s hint-conditioned token predictions only there, alongside ordinary rewards. In their coding setup, Markdown reward is 0.85 ± 0.09 versus 0.00 ± 0.00 for GRPO, while coding pass-rate is 0.33 ± 0.05 versus 0.33 ± 0.07; findings are limited to this setting and designed feedback.

hot.title: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI Inference
hot.summary: TKCC enables agents to optimize inference deployments as workloads change by hot-reloading candidate forward passes in a persistent engine, screening them before representative measurements. Its cost model selects GPU-parallelism configurations. On B200 GLM 5.3, two-tier measurement evaluated 1,354 candidates versus 168 for a single slow tier and found a 7.2% faster solution; the result is specific to that comparison.

hot.title: GSBR: Geometric Support Behavior Regularization for Online RL
hot.summary: GSBR guides online robot learning by penalizing actions only outside neighborhoods around sampled actions from a pretrained controller. This lets the actor choose among supported behaviors while permitting nearby improvements at a distance-based cost. Across 19 tasks in four benchmarks, GSBR averages 95% success and 0.95 normalized throughput, versus RLT’s 0.77; on LIBERO, RLT has higher success.

hot.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
hot.summary: FrontierPhysics evaluates whether AI agents can conduct open-ended physics research from high-level briefs. The benchmark uses physicist-contributed research tasks and grades structured outputs with deterministic checks, alongside manuscripts and research trajectories against expert-authored rubrics. Passing requires all verifier tests and blocking criteria. The top tested configuration passed 46/168 trials (27.4%), measuring performance under this protocol rather than human publication acceptance.

hot.title: You don't need long context
hot.summary: The authors test whether agents need full histories or documents in active context using compact handoff states and tool-based retrieval. In long-horizon and long-input tasks these approaches preserve or improve results. For Qwen 3 Coder Next, a 16K rather than 256K context window yielded 7× more decoded tokens per second; this measures throughput, not task time, and evidence is limited.

hot.title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
hot.summary: The authors use speculative decoding to steer selected decisions into less noisy context positions. A trained draft is more likely to be rejected at those points, so the target resamples at the start of a fresh verification block while preserving its token distribution. On DeepSWE, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 pass rate rises from 60.6% to 67.6%; not all benchmark gains are statistically established.

hot.title: On the Volume Conjectures for Dehn-Filled 3-Manifolds Along Fundamental Shadow Link Complements With Big Volume
hot.summary: The authors prove large-level asymptotics for Reshetikhin–Turaev invariants of hyperbolic 3-manifolds obtained by integral Dehn filling fundamental shadow link complements. They extend quantum 6j symbols and use approximate reflection symmetry to cancel problematic Fourier coefficients while preserving asymptotics. Both conjectures hold at positive odd levels when manifold volume is sufficiently close to the starting complement’s; this does not cover all fillings.

hot.title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
hot.summary: ToolSpace builds executable cross-service task paths from observed tool-call traces, linking adjacent calls through data, state, and retry dependencies. It samples paths whose inputs are available, replays them from initial states, and retains those passing checks. ToolSpace-35B-A3B averages 41.0 across seven benchmarks, versus 23.0 for its backbone and 43.2 after on-policy RL; replay validates chains, not agent success.

hot.title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
hot.summary: DreamX transfers motion from human videos to robot actions without paired human–robot training data. It uses learnable queries to read a pretrained video model’s features and compress motion into a code, which can condition future-video generation or robot action prediction. On LARYBench, it achieves 0.17 average normalized action MSE and 69.67% accuracy; transfer is demonstrated only in evaluated open-loop settings.

hot.title: Introducing Ripple-65B Preview, a Frontier Open-Weight Model
hot.summary: Ricursive Intelligence releases Ripple-65B Preview, a general-purpose variant of the proprietary language model that powers its AI chip design platform. The dense 65B model was trained from scratch on 12 trillion tokens with up to 1M context, and reaches 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1, a new U.S. open-weight state of the art for agentic coding. The full R&D cost was $32M, which the team estimates is one-tenth that of the previous open-weight SOTA.

hot.title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
hot.summary: NEO-VLA combines image patches and language in one backbone and lets an action expert read selected layers to generate continuous action chunks. In frozen-backbone LIBERO evaluation, it reaches 90.9% average success, versus 79.5% for Qwen3-VL 2B. The comparison does not isolate encoder removal as the cause, and performance under object-position perturbations falls to 3.0%.

hot.title: Meta$^2$: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents
hot.summary: Meta² teaches an evolver reusable guidance for changing a frozen model’s task harness during a run, rather than selecting one harness for every task. Its Meta-Skill guides when to edit, hold, or avoid changes; edits remain run-local, without held-out verifier feedback. With GPT-5.6-Terra, it reports mean@5 81.00% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and mean@3 44.44% on DeepSWE 1.1, on two tested benchmarks.

hot.title: Hybrid Particle-Voxel Dynamics for Multimodal 3D World Simulation
hot.summary: 3D World Simulator predicts robot-manipulated scenes in a shared 3D representation, encoding camera-derived point clouds into voxel latents and decoding predicted states into geometry, renderable images, and tactile points. On six ALOHA tasks, its 200-frame open-loop PSNR is 23.24 versus 20.59 for Robot4DGen. On held-out Deform360 objects, geometry improves over particle baselines, but image metrics are worse.

hot.title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights
hot.summary: The authors show that GPT-6 Astra, a general-purpose frontier LLM, can read and write neural network weights directly, without gradient descent or trained helper models. Across eight experiments it identifies what small networks were trained on from their weights, fixes and writes game-playing policies, and edits 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights to stop reasoning loops. They call this Weight-Space Programming.

hot.title: Hinted Scaling Laws
hot.summary: The authors develop benchmark hinting to forecast downstream accuracy when smaller models score near zero. They add graded solution help, fit its relationship with model scale, and predict the unhinted score. On Delphi, logit mixing predicted 25.9% GSM8K accuracy for a 10^23-FLOP model within 3 percentage points, using models trained with at most 10^20 FLOPs. This result uses a solution-prompted teacher.

hot.title: Behind Video Generation: Observations and Insights on Multimodal Understanding from Kling
hot.summary: The authors present an understanding stack for video generation that links dense captioning, reference-grounded captioning, prompt enhancement, text encoding, reward modeling, and evaluation. Their Kling captioner scores 21.70 on VidCapBench accuracy, while a smaller variant scores 21.84. In one staged prompt-enhancement setup, StoryEval rises from 65.42 to 76.46; DiT-in-the-loop reinforcement learning improves worst-case quality but can reduce best-case output quality.

hot.title: VABAR: A Variational Automation Benchmark for Agentic Robotics
hot.summary: VABAR evaluates agentic robot programs across six simulated tasks with structured, physically feasible variations. It uses reusable perception, planning, and control skills, and records success and diagnostics. On Gear Meshing Level 1, autonomously generated GaP succeeds on 70.0% of instances, versus 0.0% for Claude Code and 100.0% for a human-authored graph; these results are simulated, not evidence of real-world operation.

hot.title: PyRUA-DataFarm: LLM Agent as a Cost-Efficient Teleoperator for Real-Ready Robot Data
hot.summary: DataFarm uses a coding agent to build a simulation task from a request and a calibration recording, then generates action-labelled episodes whose actions are rendered as synchronized camera views. The recording’s actions are not reused. On one dual-arm robot, farm-only policies achieved 87 successes versus 46 for teleoperation-trained policies in 100 trials across five tasks under unseen appearance conditions.

hot.title: Non-Unitary Quantum Butterfly Effect: Theory and Experiment
hot.summary: The authors track local perturbations with circuit echoes and an out-of-time-order correlator (OTOC), analyzing Haar-random brickwork circuits with measurements modeled as dephasing. Measurements leave a causal front visible but attenuate the signal inside it; sparse-measurement theory predicts a decay timescale proportional to p^(-1/2) in the thermodynamic Gaussian regime. An eight-qubit trapped-ion demonstration resolves structure, but does not validate the prediction.

hot.title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
hot.summary: IdeaTaste tests whether AI research agents make choices resembling those of human communities. It generates proposals from literature frozen at the end of 2025, then compares their citations and ideas with papers published in January–August 2026. Agents reach about 26% of human level on citation matching and 18% on idea matching, but publication similarity measures community choices, not objective research quality.

likes.title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
likes.summary: The authors cast pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning, and suitable reinforcement-learning updates as maximum-likelihood training with a changing data mixture. In reasoning experiments, unified schedules reach higher accuracy and coverage at larger tested compute budgets, though staged training can lead at intermediate budgets. After coding updates, a 0.76B model with 5% midtraining-data mixing scores 58.47% pass@16 versus 52.12%, limited to this continuation setup.

likes.title: Mistral Large 4
likes.summary: Mistral Large 4 is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model whose authors examine long-context attention for agentic coding. They find architecture variants with similar language-modeling loss can differ on SWE-bench Verified, while knowledge-based evaluations show no analogous gap. The final system restores long-context access in more layers and uses DSA to select past tokens; its benchmark results do not isolate DSA’s effect.

likes.title: How to Loop Your Transformer: Loop Scaling, Specialization, and Parallel Inference
likes.summary: The authors study looping, which reuses transformer weights for repeated computation, in dense decoder-only models. They compare loop designs and shifted parallel looping. In tested over-trained conditions, two-loop models at 80 tokens per parameter reach a given DCLM validation bits-per-byte with fewer training FLOPs than vanilla models at 160 tokens per parameter, without establishing general efficiency or latency gains.

likes.title: Training language models in simulation for psychiatric intake
likes.summary: The simulation-trained model improves psychiatric intake conversations by practicing multi-turn encounters with simulated patients and receiving rewards for clinical reasoning, communication, and safety. In a randomized, double-blind crossover study, it received higher psychiatrist transcript ratings than its identically prompted base model in 46 of 60 matched scenario pairs (76.7%). This supports improvement in controlled text encounters, not real-patient safety or effectiveness.

likes.title: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models
likes.summary: The authors evaluate ten frozen visual representations for whether small probes can read visible scene structure, retain objects after they leave view, predict spatial updates under camera motion, and select goal-directed actions. VideoMAE’s out-of-view bearing error is 36.45°, versus DINOv2’s 65.38°, despite DINOv2’s stronger visible-scene readouts. These offline tests do not establish online memory or reliable robot behavior.

likes.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
likes.summary: ID-WM separates choosing intermediate states from choosing actions to make long-horizon planning in world models manageable. A diffusion model proposes nearby subgoals, and an action-conditioned model searches for actions to reach them, with planning repeated locally. In state-based PushT random-goal trials, it succeeds in 77% versus 21% for single-level world-model MPC; this result is limited to the tested benchmark setting.

likes.title: Hinted Scaling Laws
likes.summary: The authors develop benchmark hinting to forecast downstream accuracy when smaller models score near zero. They add graded solution help, fit its relationship with model scale, and predict the unhinted score. On Delphi, logit mixing predicted 25.9% GSM8K accuracy for a 10^23-FLOP model within 3 percentage points, using models trained with at most 10^20 FLOPs. This result uses a solution-prompted teacher.

likes.title: On the Generalization Limitation of On-Policy Distillation for Post-RL Consolidation
likes.summary: The authors test whether on-policy distillation transfers specialist improvements beyond supervised tasks. A student learns from its own responses with teacher guidance; multi-teacher training routes domains to matching teachers. Narrow math supervision nearly matches teacher scores in-distribution but leaves out-of-distribution performance 3.73% below base. Broader data with a stronger teacher raises scores across five benchmarks, but effects are not isolated.

likes.title: L3G-World: Real-Time Infinite World Generation with Latent 3D Gaussian Memory
likes.summary: L3G-World generates interactive video worlds using a revisable 3D Gaussian scene memory that stores video-VAE features. It renders this memory into latent conditioning for each video chunk, then updates it by adding missing content and refining visible Gaussians. On DL3DV loop-closure tests, it achieves 16.00 self-consistency PSNR versus 13.96 for Spatia; Matrix-Game 3.0 has lower LPIPS, and tests use static scenes.

likes.title: Rethinking Pre-pretraining
likes.summary: The authors test whether synthetic pre-pretraining (PPT) is a better use of a fixed training-compute budget than natural-language training. They compare synthetic-first and natural-language-only training across scarce-data, plentiful-data, and high-token regimes. Across these tested compute-matched settings, synthetic PPT does not outperform natural-language training on language modeling; this finding is limited to the tested recipes and evaluations.

likes.title: Automating AI R&D for Molecular Discovery
likes.summary: Intology evaluates Locus, its autonomous AI R&D system, on three molecular discovery tasks: proprietary molecular property prediction, adapting Boltz-2 for small-molecule potency prediction, and designing antibody workflows around BoltzGen/Boltz-2 and ESMC/ESMFold2. Under matched compute, Locus outperforms Claude Code, Codex, and baselines from Boltz and BioHub, generalizing better from limited data and finding more sample-efficient solutions.

likes.title: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention
likes.summary: The authors introduce Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), which groups similar keys and searches group representatives before retrieving selected original keys for attention. Its Flat variant scans all group centroids, while Tree uses hierarchical search. On GLM-5.3-FLASH, Flat makes one layer’s prefill 22.7× faster at 10M tokens than the model’s sparse-attention baseline; this is not an end-to-end speedup.

likes.title: Scale Bounds and Force-Class Obstructions to Physically Realizing OpenAI’s Forced Navier–Stokes Blowup
likes.summary: The authors assess forces supporting OpenAI’s forced-blowup construction and quantify its leading profile’s scale. Assuming the construction meets the stated flow hypotheses, they exclude singularities for specified force classes, including forces whose curl satisfies a unique-continuation condition. For water at molecular core length, the matching radius exceeds 1.63×10¹² Hubble radii; this leading-profile bound does not establish laboratory-time accuracy.

likes.title: Gym-Anything for Robotics: Scaling physical simulations with digital agents
likes.summary: Gym-Anything for Robotics uses coding agents to build robotics simulations and tasks, then separate auditors test their evidence and probe for defects. The system selects 120 action groups and builds 25 simulations, forming 200 RoboWorld environments. Claude Opus 5.5 succeeds on 0% of 25 test tasks, while reaching 32% on an easier training subset; these are simulated tasks, not real-robot results.

likes.title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
likes.summary: SpecSlot assigns global communication to low-frequency image carriers while keeping finer output slots local. Each anchor produces multiple slots with disjoint spectral roles, but only one joins dense global attention. On ImageNet-512 it reaches 9.14 FID versus 11.98 for a FLOPs-matched JiT-CM control, with 3.9% fewer conditional forward FLOPs; it remains 0.69 FID worse than JiT-B/16.

likes.title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
likes.summary: The authors introduce uni-robot-agent, a shared robot-interaction harness that lets adapters translate common tools and execution feedback across models and environments. On RoboDojo, open-weight Qwen3.8-Flash-Next scores 31.39 without privileged simulator inputs, above the published GPT-6 Astra–RoboProbe score of 28.97; this is not a matched comparison, since evaluations used 252 and 2,100 episodes, respectively.

likes.title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
likes.summary: IdeaTaste tests whether AI research agents make choices resembling those of human communities. It generates proposals from literature frozen at the end of 2025, then compares their citations and ideas with papers published in January–August 2026. Agents reach about 26% of human level on citation matching and 18% on idea matching, but publication similarity measures community choices, not objective research quality.

likes.title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
likes.summary: The authors survey agent harnesses as runtime layers that connect video production, interaction with video world models, and system development. They explain how harnesses select context, schedule tools, maintain state, route feedback, and enforce budgets. The framework organizes prior work and evaluation requirements, but no surveyed system shows revised development procedures improve later rounds of video-generator development.
